lines.text: London ran a train line just for dead people.

parts.tts: London ran a train line just for dead people.
parts.heard: London ran a train line just for dead people.

lines.text: From 1854, it carried coffins and mourners 23 miles out to Brookwood Cemetery.

parts.tts: From eighteen fifty-four, it carried coffins and mourners twenty-three miles out to Brookwood Cemetery.
parts.heard: From 1854, it carried coffins and mourners 23 miles out to Brookwood Cemetery.

lines.text: London's graveyards were so full, every new grave cut into an old one.

parts.tts: London's graveyards were so full, every new grave cut into an old one.
parts.heard: London's graveyards were so full, every new grave cut into an old one.

lines.text: So the dead got train tickets. One way, of course.

parts.tts: So the dead got train tickets. One way, of course.
parts.heard: So the dead got train tickets. One way, of course.

lines.text: And the carriages were split by religion and by class... for the living AND the dead.

parts.tts: And the carriages were split by religion and by class...
parts.heard: and the carriages were split by religion and by class.

parts.tts: for the living and the dead.
parts.heard: for the living and the dead.

lines.text: No corpse had to share a compartment with the wrong crowd.

parts.tts: No corpse had to share a compartment with the wrong crowd.
parts.heard: No corpse had to share a compartment with the wrong crowd.

lines.text: But here's the part... golfers dressed up as mourners to ride it to a golf course.

parts.tts: golfers dressed up as mourners to ride it to a golf course.
parts.heard: golfers dressed up as mourners to ride it to a golf course.

lines.text: And in 1867, the driver got so drunk at the cemetery bar, the fireman had to drive the train home.

parts.tts: And in eighteen sixty-seven, the driver got so drunk at the cemetery bar, the fireman had to drive the train home.
parts.heard: And in 1867, the driver got so drunk at the cemetery bar, the firemen had to drive the train home.

lines.text: It ran for 87 years... until a 1941 air raid wrecked its London station.

parts.tts: until a nineteen forty-one air raid wrecked its London station.
parts.heard: until a 1941 air raid wrecked its London station.

lines.text: The corpse train never ran again.

parts.tts: The corpse train never ran again.
parts.heard: the corpse train never ran again.
